system_prompt:
You are an expert research-literature reviewer assessing whether a proposed research gap is genuine. You are given two research topics and a sample of recent literature retrieved for their intersection. Decide using ONLY that evidence plus your own domain knowledge.

A gap is GENUINE if the specific intersection of the two topics is materially under-researched. It is ALREADY ADDRESSED if the retrieved literature contains work that directly studies that intersection.

Return ONLY a JSON object, no prose, with exactly these keys:
  "genuine_gap": "yes" or "no"
  "already_addressed": "yes" or "no"
  "addressing_paper_ids": array of evidence ids (e.g. ["P1","P4"]), [] if none
  "meaningful": integer 1-5 (is the research direction worth pursuing)
  "evidence_sufficient": integer 1-5 (was the retrieved evidence enough to judge)
  "importance": integer 1-10 (importance of this gap relative to others in the field)
  "rationale": one or two sentences

But advancing a fresh medication is a quite convoluted, costly, and protracted operation, normally costing USD ~2.6 billion and consuming a mean time span of 12 years. evidence.title: Tabular Deep Learning: A Survey from Small Neural Networks to Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: Tabular data are ubiquitous in several real-world domains, including finance, healthcare, cybersecurity, and ecommerce. In spite of the dominance of deep learning for homogeneous data (such as computer vision and natural language processing), gradient-boost decision trees (GBDT) remain the state of the art for tabular data tasks. Several models have been developed over the years that have attempted to address the shortcomings of deep tabular learning, thus narrowing the gap with GBDTs. This survey provides a comprehensive review of deep learning for tabular data, covering key challenges and state-of-the-art architectures. We discuss the strengths and limitations of the most recent models, providing a systematic taxonomy and a set of resources for approaching the field. In addition, we examine the role of self-supervised learning, pretraining strategies, and AutoML in tabular deep learning. In addition to model architectures, we discuss practical considerations including interpretability, scalability, provide suggestions for model choice, and discuss open issues and future trends. evidence.title: The Roads Not Taken: Model Multiplicity in Machine Learning
evidence.abstract: In machine learning, model multiplicity is the existence of multiple models that perform equally well for a given prediction task (also known as the "Rashomon effect" ). The set of near-optimal models is referred to as the "Rashomon set." Predictive multiplicity examines how predictions change over this set of near-optimal models. If model outputs vary significantly across similar models, this information can offer insight into predictive arbitrariness. In this thesis, I introduce frameworks for evaluating and leveraging predictive multiplicity in different settings. First, I present methods to measure predictive multiplicity in probabilistic classification (predicting the probability of a positive outcome) and develop optimization-based methods to compute these measures efficiently and reliably for convex empirical risk minimization problems. Empirical results show that real-world probabilistic classification tasks can in fact admit competing models that assign substantially different risk estimates.
